[[File:PhilipsArenafrom303.jpg|thumb|The Thrashers played their home games at the [[State Farm Arena|Philips Arena]] since their inaugural season.]]
The [[Atlanta Thrashers]] were an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. They played in the [[Southeast Division (NHL)|Southeast Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) for its entire history. They moved to [[Winnipeg]], Manitoba in 2011 and became the 2nd Incarnation of the [[Winnipeg Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-28}}</ref> The team joined the NHL in 1999 as an [[expansion team]]. The Thrashers played their home games at the [[Philips Arena]] since their inaugural season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thrashers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=14045|title=Thrashers Franchise Timeline|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|accessdate=2008-12-28|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100324145811/http://thrashers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page|archivedate=2010-03-24}}</ref> The Thrashers were owned by [[Atlanta Spirit, LLC]], and [[Rick Dudley]] was their [[general manager]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thrashers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=13838|title=Front Office / Staff Listing|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|accessdate=2008-12-28|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218193859/http://thrashers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=13838|archivedate=2008-12-18}}</ref>

There were five Thrashers [[head coach]]es during their existence. The team's first head coach was [[Curt Fraser]], who coached for three seasons. [[Bob Hartley]] is the franchise's all-time leader for the most regular-season games coached (291), the most regular-season game wins (136), the most regular-season [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] (309), and the only Thrashers head coach to coach any post-season games (4). All of the Thrashers head coaches except for Hartley have spent their entire NHL head coaching careers with the Thrashers. [[John Anderson (ice hockey, born 1957)|John Anderson]] was the head coach of the Thrashers from 2008 to 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/ATL/coaches.html|title=Atlanta Thrashers Coach Register|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|accessdate=2008-12-28}}</ref> [[Craig Ramsay]] was the last head coach of the Thrashers.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120313195521/http://www.philipsarena.com/Resources/GeneralInfo/Thrashers_Update.htm?id=532663 nhl.com] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200524183113/http://http//thrashers.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=532663%2F |date=May 24, 2020 }} in English</ref>

==Notes==
*{{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Thrashers. Thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
*{{note label|Note2|b|b}} Before the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|title=Official Rules|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-28|format=PDF|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511234846/http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|archivedate=2008-05-11}}</ref>
